stem: In audiology, what do the circle (O) and cross (X) symbols represent on an audiogram?

options.text: Circle for the right ear, cross for the left ear
Circle for air conduction, cross for bone conduction
Circle for normal hearing, cross for pathological hearing
Circle for pediatric patients, cross for adult patients

explanation: This is the standardized notation mentioned in the lecture: circles denote right ear results and crosses denote left ear results.
rationale: These symbols are the standard way to distinguish between the two sides of the head.

optionExplanations.A: This is the standardized notation mentioned in the lecture: circles denote right ear results and crosses denote left ear results.
optionExplanations.B: Air and bone conduction use different symbols (like brackets for bone), while circle/cross specifically differentiate the sides.
optionExplanations.C: Symbols indicate which ear is being tested, regardless of whether the hearing level is normal or impaired.
optionExplanations.D: Audiogram symbols are standardized across all age groups to indicate right and left ears.

source.hint: These symbols are the standard way to distinguish between the two sides of the head.
